alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction lowers DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70% and recommend using valproic acid instead. Patient started carbamazepine 400 mg twice daily two weeks ago while on DTG-based TLD. Viral load rose from <50 copies/mL (September 2025) to 1,240 copies/mL today, with adherence reported good. The temporal relationship between carbamazepine initiation and viral load rebound strongly supports a drug interaction causing reduced DTG exposure. The guideline explicitly advises using valproic acid rather than carbamazepine in patients on DTG. This interaction likely explains the treatment failure despite reported adherence.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid per guideline recommendation, or consult neurology for alternative antiepileptic. Repeat viral load after interaction resolved.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatremia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), with symptoms of ataxia, nystagmus, tremor, dizziness, and headaches. Sodium is 128 mmol/L, consistent with carbamazepine-induced hyponatremia. The clinician plans dose reduction and repeat level, which is appropriate. Both carbamazepine and valproate can contribute to CNS toxicity; however, the supra-therapeutic carbamazepine level and recent initiation strongly support carbamazepine as the primary cause. Hyponatremia may also worsen neurological symptoms. Close monitoring of sodium and neurological status during dose adjustment is essential.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, monitor sodium and carbamazepine levels closely, and review with neurology for alternative agent given DTG interaction.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires repeat testing
alerts.message: Guidelines define treatment failure as two consecutive viral load results >1,000 copies/mL. Patient's viral load is 1,240 copies/mL today after prior suppression. A single detectable result does not yet confirm treatment failure, but guidelines note viral load >200 copies/mL carries risk of transmission and subsequent virologic non-suppression. An early repeat viral load is needed to determine if this represents true treatment failure or transient viremia. The carbamazepine-DTG interaction is a likely reversible cause. Adherence should be reassessed.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat viral load after addressing carbamazepine-DTG interaction. If still >1,000 copies/mL, confirm treatment failure and switch regimen per guidelines.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT with hepatotoxic polypharmacy
alerts.message: Patient's ALT is 68 U/L, which may be Grade 1 elevation depending on the lab's ULN. Patient is concurrently taking carbamazepine, valproate, and TDF—all associated with hepatotoxicity. The recent carbamazepine initiation and supra-therapeutic level make carbamazepine a likely contributor. Valproate is also a known hepatotoxin. TDF less commonly causes transaminase elevation. Guidelines recommend liver function tests based on clinical indication for patients on potentially hepatotoxic medications. Monitoring trend and evaluating for drug-induced liver injury is warranted.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat ALT and monitor liver function trend. If ALT worsens or exceeds Grade 2, consider holding offending agent and hepatology review.

Consolidated Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of HIV and Aids in Uganda - 2022 ## 6.5 FIRST-LINE ART REGIMENS FOR PATIENTS INITIATING ART Principles for selecting the ARV regimens (treatment optimization): The first-line ART regimens for treating HIV infection in Uganda were selected based on the universal principles: * Toxicity: regimens with less toxicity are preferred. * Palatability and pill burden; better palatability and lower pill burden preferred. * Increased durability and efficacy. * Sequencing: spares other available formulations for use in the 2nd line regimen. * Harmonization of regimen across age and population. * Lower cost. DOLUTEGRAVIR (DTG) is an integrase inhibitor and is recommended for use as the anchor ARV in the preferred first, second- and third-line treatment regimens for all recipients of care such as children, adolescents, men, women including pregnant women, breastfeeding women, adolescent girls and women of childbearing potential). **RATIONALE FOR USING DOLUTEGRAVIR (DTG)** a. Consolidated Guidelines for the Prevention and Treatment of HIV and Aids in Uganda - 2022 virological monitoring provides an early and more accurate indication of treatment failure and indicates the need to switch from first line to second-line drugs, and from second- line to third-line drugs, toward reducing accumulation of drug-resistance mutations and improved clinical outcomes. Dolutegravir (DTG)-based regimens (e.g., tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir [TLD]) have increased viral load suppression (VLS) rates to unprecedented levels, hence a need to actively monitor patients for low-level viremia to keep DTG a durable treatment option for as long as possible. Furthermore, low-level viraemia monitoring can enhances monitoring of achieving and sustaining HIV epidemic control, as viral load of >200 copies/mL is associated with potential risk of sexual transmission as well as subsequent virologic non-suppression and treatment failure.
